speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these mental status changes began and if there have been any recent changes to your medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any fever, headache, or neck stiffness in the last few days? Do you have any history of liver disease or alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of liver disease, alcohol use, or recent exposure to toxins? I also need to know if you have experienced any fever, headache, or neck stiffness recently.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Patient has a history of hypertension, managed with medication. No other significant medical history is reported. Social history: Patient is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Drinks alcohol socially. No illicit drug use is reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's smoking history and progressive confusion, I need to rule out hypoxia or metabolic derangements. REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since metabolic and blood gas tests are normal, I need to rule out structural brain abnormalities or infection. REQUEST TEST: Non-contrast CT Head, Lumbar Puncture.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal metabolic, blood gas, and structural brain imaging results, I need to investigate other causes of encephalopathy. Have you experienced any recent seizures, witnessed or unwitnessed, and are you currently taking any psychiatric medications or benzodiazepines?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, seizure, vision changes, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, recent illness, or fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any tremors, difficulty walking, or changes in your speech? I also need to know if you have been exposed to any potential toxins, such as carbon monoxide from a faulty heater or well water, or if you have had recent dental work.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, seizure, vision changes, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, recent illness, or fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am concerned about carbon monoxide poisoning given the normal workup and smoking history; have you checked your home's carbon monoxide detectors or experienced any recent headaches or nausea with others in your household? REQUEST TEST: Carboxyhemoglobin_level, Methemoglobin_level.

speaker: Doctor
text: With all structural, metabolic, infectious, and toxicological causes ruled out, I suspect a psychogenic etiology given the normal workup. DIAGNOSIS READY: Conversion Disorder
